frontmatter_raw:
name: add-agent-memory
description: Wire Redis Agent Memory into an existing agent with redis-iris so it remembers users across sessions. Asks five questions (what to remember, what to share, what never to keep, how long to keep it, whether users can be forgotten), writes the answers to service.yaml, provisions the service from the terminal with `iris agent-memory service create`, then wires recall and write-back into the agent's turn in any framework. Use when the agent forgets users, uses InMemoryStore or a checkpointer only, keeps memory in a dict or local DB, or the user asks for long-term memory, recall, or right-to-erasure.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: redis
  version: "1.0.0"

name: add-agent-playbooks
description: Add Redis Iris Agent Playbooks to an existing agent. Use when approved answers or repeatable procedures live in prompts, document retrieval, or a semantic response cache. Connect or provision a Playbook, publish FAQs and Skills, and verify the first application turn with optional review proposals.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: redis
  version: "1.0.0"

name: add-context-gateway
description: Put the MCP servers an existing agent uses behind one Redis Iris Context Gateway with redis-iris, so the agent connects to one MCP endpoint with one agent key instead of configuring each server and its secret. Asks whether the Gateway is in Redis Cloud or self-managed, then five questions (which MCP servers and secrets the agent has today, how many tools it sees, which read-only tools may be cached, which tools return large results, whether the framework speaks MCP itself). Self-managed, it provisions the Gateway and its Upstreams from the terminal with `iris context-gateway` and sets cache and compression policies. In Redis Cloud the developer creates them in the console. Then it points the agent at the Gateway in any framework and verifies it with `tools list` and `tools call`. Use when the agent configures several MCP servers one by one, carries one secret per server, loads too many tool schemas into the prompt, or the user asks for Context Gateway, one MCP endpoint, tool caching, or result handles.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: redis
  version: "1.0.0"

name: add-intent-router
description: Replace an existing agent's hand-written routing (keyword if/else chains, regex, or an LLM call that only picks a route) with a Redis Iris Intent Router through redis-iris, so a message maps to a defined intent and its dispatch target by example phrasings and a score threshold. Asks five questions (what the routes are today, a few real phrasings per route, what each route dispatches to, what happens when nothing matches, which embedding model), writes the answers to intents.yaml, provisions the Router from the terminal with `iris intent-router service create`, loads the intents with `iris intent-router intents add`, then wires `router.match()` where the agent decides today. Use when the agent routes with keywords or an extra LLM call, or the user asks for intent detection, intent routing, or semantic routing.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: redis
  version: "1.0.0"

name: add-lens
description: Add Redis Iris Lens tracing to an existing AI agent through redis-iris, so every agent turn is one trace in the Lens UI with its LLM calls, tokens, tool calls, memory and document retrievals, and which of them entered the prompt. Detects how the agent runs (LangGraph or ADK attach, workflows.turn, another framework, or a plain loop), installs redis-iris[llm-tracing], calls lens.init(agent_id=...), opens one lens.turn() per turn where Iris does not open it already, and covers coexistence with an OpenTelemetry setup or LLM instrumentation the app already has. Use when the user asks to add Lens, tracing, observability, or per-turn traces to their agent, or asks why their Lens traces are missing.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: redis
  version: "1.0.0"

name: add-redis-iris
description: Add Redis Iris to an existing AI agent in any framework (LangGraph, LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, Pydantic AI, CrewAI, or a plain loop). Use when the user asks to add Iris, Redis Agent Memory, Agent Playbooks, Context Gateway, Intent Router, or Lens to their agent, or asks which Iris product their agent needs. Detects the framework and routes to the product skill.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: redis
  version: "1.0.0"

name: redis-clustering
description: Redis Cluster and replication guidance covering hash tags for multi-key operations, avoiding CROSSSLOT errors, and reading from replicas to scale read-heavy workloads. Use when designing keys for a sharded Redis Cluster, debugging CROSSSLOT errors on MGET / SDIFF / pipelines, configuring a multi-key transaction in a cluster, or routing reads to replicas for caches, analytics, or dashboards.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: Redis, Inc.
  version: "0.1.0"

name: redis-connections
description: Redis client and connection guidance covering connection pooling, multiplexing, pipelining, client-side caching with RESP3, avoiding slow commands (KEYS, SMEMBERS, HGETALL), and tuning socket timeouts. Use when configuring a Redis client (redis-py, Jedis, Lettuce, NRedisStack), batching commands for throughput, eliminating per-request connection creation, iterating large keyspaces with SCAN, enabling client-side caching for read-heavy workloads, or setting connect and read timeouts.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: Redis, Inc.
  version: "0.1.0"

name: redis-core
description: Core Redis modeling guidance — choose the right data structure (String, Hash, List, Set, Sorted Set, JSON, Stream, Vector Set) and use consistent colon-separated key names. Use when designing a Redis data model, caching objects, deciding between Hash and JSON, building counters, leaderboards, membership sets, or session stores, or when reviewing/cleaning up Redis key naming.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: Redis, Inc.
  version: "0.1.0"

name: redis-docs-mcp
description: >-
  Working with the redis-docs MCP server (search / fetch / ask at redis.io/mcp) — how its index is
  shaped and how to read what it returns. Use when those tools are available and you are about to
  look something up in the Redis documentation, or when a result is confusing — fetch returned one
  short section instead of a page, several hits share one url, ids look like #sec:w1,
  metadata.version reads 1.0.0, a search came back empty, or ask was rate-limited or said the docs
  do not cover it. Also covers what redis.io does and does not index.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: Redis, Inc.
  version: "0.1.0"

name: redis-observability
description: Redis observability guidance — which metrics to monitor (memory, connections, hit ratio, ops/sec, rejected connections), which built-in commands to reach for during incident triage (SLOWLOG, INFO, MEMORY DOCTOR, CLIENT LIST, FT.PROFILE), and when to use the Redis Insight GUI. Use when setting up monitoring or alerts for a Redis instance, diagnosing a performance regression, profiling a slow FT.SEARCH query, or wiring Redis metrics into Prometheus, Datadog, or similar.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: Redis, Inc.
  version: "0.1.0"

name: redis-search
description: Redis Search guidance covering FT.CREATE schema design, field type selection (TEXT, TAG, NUMERIC, GEO, GEOSHAPE, VECTOR, JSON path), DIALECT 2 query syntax, FT.SEARCH / FT.AGGREGATE / FT.HYBRID command selection, vector similarity with HNSW or FLAT, hybrid retrieval combining lexical and vector ranking, RAG pipelines, zero-downtime index updates via aliases, and debugging with FT.PROFILE and FT.EXPLAIN. Use when defining a search index on Hash or JSON documents, writing FT.SEARCH queries with filters, sorting, aggregation, or vector KNN, tuning HNSW parameters, building a RAG retrieval pipeline, or troubleshooting slow or empty search results.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: Redis, Inc.
  version: "1.0.0"

name: redis-security
description: Redis security guidance covering authentication (requirepass and ACL users), TLS, ACL-based least-privilege access control, restricting network exposure via bind and protected-mode, firewall rules, and disabling dangerous commands. Use when deploying Redis to production, defining ACL users for an application, configuring TLS connections, locking down a Redis instance behind a firewall, or auditing a Redis deployment for security hardening.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: Redis, Inc.
  version: "0.1.0"

name: redis-semantic-cache
description: Redis LangCache guidance for semantic caching of LLM responses on Redis Cloud — calling search/set via the SDK or REST API, tuning the similarity threshold, separating caches per task type, and filtering with custom attributes. Use when caching LLM completions or RAG answers to cut API cost and latency, building a cache-aside layer in front of OpenAI / Anthropic / etc., tuning hit rate vs precision, or splitting one app's LLM workloads into multiple LangCache caches.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: Redis, Inc.
  version: "0.1.0"
